To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Na partitions to PbS precipitates in a PbTe solid solution matrix and segregates at matrix/precipitated interfaces, inducing morphologically anisotropy.
the addition of Na to PbTe-PbI(2) matrix/precipitates system results in a change of PbS morphology from irregular to cuboidal and truncated cubic shapes.
Na segregates to (100) PbS/PbTe interfaces and lowers the interfacial energy of the PbTe/PbTe(100) interface, resulting in a cuboidal morphology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a fundamental understanding of phase separation in PbTe-based materials, with an emphasis on the effects of Na doping on the phase separation process.
the fundamental question of how to control morphology of nanosized precipitates in a matrix material.
the control of morphology in nanostructured materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the addition of Na in PbTe matrix induces the formation of faceted PbS nanostructures by segregation of Na at the matrix/ precipitate interface, which is in contrast to the formation of irregularly shaped nanostructures in undoped PbTe.
the addition of sodium as a solute to the PbTe matrix results in a decrease in the interfacial energy between the matrix and the precipitate.
the addition of Na to the PbTe-PbI(2) matrix results in a change in the surface energy anisotropy and the morphology of the precipitates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we demonstrate the role of a third element in controlling morphology evolution in a solid-state system.
the morphology of nanocrystals can be tuned by the segregation and partitioning of a ternary solute at the matrix/phase boundary.
we show how to control morphology in a matrix/precipitates system by using a ternary addition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the addition of a ternary solute can be used as an effective means of controlling the morphological evolution of precipitates in solid-state systems, which can be exploited in a wide variety of systems.
the addition of a ternary solute (Na) to a PbTe matrix can control the morphology of the precipitating PbS phase.
a ternary element, which partitions differently between the precipitate and the matrix, can be used to control morphological evolution of nanostructures during solid-state phase transformations.
